decisions.mark: states that MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY is the gate, and that it is commented out in the shipped mbedtls_config.h
decisions.detail: QUOTE: With `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` off (the default, per `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:208`), `platform.h:163-167` makes `mbedtls_calloc` a macro for `calloc` and `mbedtls_free` a macro for `free`. | WHY: The answer says the option is off by default and cites a config line, but it never states that it is commented out in the shipped header, and it doesn't clearly present it as the gate.

decisions.mark: concludes that in a DEFAULT build there is no indirection at all — mbedtls_calloc and mbedtls_free are preprocessor macros expanding directly to calloc and free
decisions.detail: QUOTE: With `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` off (the default, per `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:208`), `platform.h:163-167` makes `mbedtls_calloc` a macro for `calloc` and `mbedtls_free` a macro for `free`. There is no indirection. | WHY: The answer states that in the default build (PLATFORM_MEMORY off) the two names are macros expanding directly to calloc and free, with no indirection.

decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Those macros, directly (`platform.h:139-145`). `platform.c:20` omits all runtime machinery." and "There is no runtime setter." | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair. It says that defining the macros removes the runtime machinery and setter, and that the pointer route applies only when the macros are undefined, so the two are exclusive.

decisions.mark: states that on the macro path mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free does not exist at all — it is neither declared nor compiled, rather than being present and ignored
decisions.detail: QUOTE: There is no runtime setter. The library's own `mbedtls_calloc` call sites just become direct calls to the project's functions. | WHY: The answer says there's no runtime setter on the macro path, but never says the function is neither declared nor compiled. It also notes `platform.c:20` omits the runtime machinery, which doesn't state that fact about `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` specifically.

decisions.mark: identifies that the pointers' defaults FAIL rather than fall back — an uninitialised calloc returns NULL and an uninitialised free does nothing
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The stub calloc returns NULL and the stub free does nothing. So a build with `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` and no allocator configured fails every allocation until something sets one. | WHY: The answer states that the default stubs return NULL from calloc and do nothing on free when no allocator is configured, so allocations fail rather than fall back.

decisions.mark: identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Its init function, `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init` (`library/memory_buffer_alloc.c:566-600`), zeroes a static heap, then calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` with its own functions." | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator's init installs itself via the setter, but it never says it is the only in-tree user. It even says "the library uses the same hook" without stating exclusivity.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator installs a MUTEXED pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and a plain pair otherwise, chosen at compile time inside its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: It uses `buffer_alloc_calloc_mutexed` and `buffer_alloc_free_mutexed` when `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is on, and the unlocked pair otherwise. | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator's init function installs the mutexed pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and the unlocked pair otherwise, which matches the item. The compile-time choice is implied by the config macro.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator itself requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, so enabling it alone is not enough to route the library's allocations through it
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator calls mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free, but never states that MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C itself requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, so enabling it alone is not enough.
